AI can already cut, caption and format a clip for you. Free GitHub skills teach Claude the editing part in minutes. So why isn't everyone going viral off podcast clips? Because editing was never the hard part. Choosing the moment is. AI does not know which 47 seconds out of a two hour conversation deserve to become the clip. No context. No content intelligence. Here is how you build that layer. Scrape the latest 100 clips from the biggest podcast short form accounts. Steven Bartlett, Chris Williamson, Alex Hormozi, anyone running serious long form volume. Capture views, post date, duration, transcript, text overlay and format. Then scrape their original long form episodes and pull the complete transcripts with timestamps. The timestamps are non negotiable. They are what lets Claude match every clip back to the exact episode and the exact moment it came from. Now you reverse engineer the decision. Why those 47 seconds. Where the clip starts. What context got removed. Whether the payoff moved forward. What spoken hook, text overlay and format they used. And how it performed against that account's normal clips. Run enough of these and the patterns surface. Turn the patterns into a Claude skill that understands how the best podcast teams select and package their clips. Then hand it any new timestamped transcript. It returns the strongest moments, exact timestamps, hook options, text overlays, formats and editing instructions. The editing skill does the easy part. None of this needs new software. The tools exist. The clipping skills exist. The data is public. Nobody is assembling it into an intelligence layer. Impossible to fail does not mean every clip goes viral. It means every clip starts with real evidence, and every result makes the next selection smarter. Build the selection layer first. The edit is the easy bit.

This Open-Source Tool Turns Your Phone System Into an AI Assistant A phone call lands on your server, and instead of a human picking up, an artificial intelligence answers it in real time. Tel Agent is an open source gateway that connects any phone line to any large language model you choose. It sits right in front of your existing phone system, letting you decide exactly who talks to a person and who talks to an agent. Because it runs entirely on your own hardware, you keep full control over your data, your recordings, and your privacy. It also handles texts, emails, and chat messages through the same brain. How to build an AI team in Claude Code — every step One AI employee is Claude Code plus three things on its desk: a job description it reads every time it wakes up, playbooks for the jobs it owns, and a notebook where its lessons go. Build that five times and you have five strangers. The team is everything you add on top. Here is the whole build, in order. 1. A desk for every employee. Each one is its own folder: job description, playbooks, notebook, working files. Nothing leaks between desks, so one glance tells you what each employee knows and owns. 2. The company folder. Three pages every employee reads the second it wakes up: one about you (how you work, what always waits for your yes), one on how the company talks, and the roster with a one-line job for each employee. Write your brand voice once and the hire you make on Friday inherits it on Friday. 3. The shared notebook. Corrections that belong to everyone (a brand rule, a platform policy, a tool nobody touches without asking) go in one notebook the whole team reads. Correct one employee Tuesday, all of them follow it Wednesday. 4. Handoffs. When a job shows up, Claude Code reads the roster one-liners and passes it to the right employee. Employees pass work down the line themselves: spin up a teammate in the background, wait for an answer, or leave a note in a teammate's inbox. You are out of the middle. 5. One board. To do, doing, done. Every employee moves its own cards and submits finished work for your review. One screen tells you who is on what. 6. A clock on every desk. One employee sorts the inbox at nine, another leaves you a trend brief each morning, another checks for approvals every half hour. The team has been at work for two hours before you wake up. 7. Fences. Each employee gets an enforced list of what it can touch (leave writing off the list and it physically cannot write a file) and a short list of what always waits for your yes: sending outside the company, spending money, deleting anything. 8. One employee whose whole job is hiring the others. Say what you need, answer three questions, and a new hire is on the roster and online in your dashboard a few minutes later. The rest of the team knows it exists before you've said a word. How it all moves, for anyone who has never written code: underneath the team sits a set of scripts. A script is a small piece of code that does one chore the same way every time. One builds a new hire's desk and adds the roster line. One carries messages between employees. One wakes each employee on its clock. One files a new playbook onto the right desk. You never open them. They fire when the moment comes. A worker runs a job. A team runs the company. This is how my own operation runs: Quill sorts the inbox, Nova reads the trends, Atlas writes the proposals, Rack keeps the servers alive, all from one shared company folder, one notebook, one board. If context, skills and notebooks are still new words to you, that's who this is for. Seven courses inside my community take you from knowing nothing to building this, in order. The platform itself, the exact code my employees run on, every one of those scripts included, is in there too: download it, open it, start hiring. Join us and start today. How to make money with AI by starting a real business — in a matter of weeks (the honest version) The exact path to making money with AI by starting a real business — no bank-account screenshots, no rich-by-Friday. Here's the whole thing: FIRST, THE CHOICE → there isn't one way, there are two — and most people who quit picked the wrong path, not the wrong dream. Path 1: the solutions business — find businesses with a boring painful problem (missed follow-ups, unanswered reviews, chased invoices), get on calls, sell the fix. Path 2: the product — build one simple thing that kills one pain, make videos about it, sell it to anyone. Scalable, no sales calls. BUILD THE DEMO → before you have a customer. Some people take a lesson, build it on their OWN use case, and in a day have a working demo. It stacks: walk into any call with a library — "oh, I've got something for that. Want to see it run?" SOLUTION FIRST, TOOLS SECOND → customers don't buy tools, they buy solutions. See the obstacle, design the system, then the technology. A tool without a solution behind it builds something that breaks. TWO ENGINES → outreach (not spraying — AI wires the tools that find the RIGHT people and personalize) or content (talk daily about the problem you solve; they reach out to you). CONSISTENCY, DONE RIGHT → two people at the same gym every day: one grinds for years eating trash — barely changes. One measures everything, adjusts, iterates — gets there every time. Same gym, same effort: one understands the system. Business is exactly this — the game pays out in month two, and most people quit in week three. MEASURE → a simple sheet: what you sent, posted, who replied. Dead numbers after a month or two = diagnose: the product, the message, or the people. Fix one, run again. #aiagents #makemoneywithai #aiautomation
